summary: Sintaxis y reglas de procesado de RDFa 1.1 (tercera edición): los atributos (vocab, typeof, property, resource, prefix…), sus tipos de valor (términos, CURIE, IRI) y cómo se resuelven a IRI. Fija pocas condiciones de documento; la conformidad de un documento HTML con RDFa la completa HTML+RDFa.
note: La conformidad de documento propia de RDFa Core (4.3) es la de XML+RDFa (text/xml, application/xml) y no aplica a una ficha servida como HTML. La conformidad de procesador (4.1, 7, 8, 10) queda fuera, salvo la recomendación a los autores de 4.1 (q04). La sintaxis de los atributos (sección 5) no lleva término de naturaleza: la recomendación de usarlos conforme a RDFa Core la da HTML+RDFa (w3c-html-rdfa#q02).

quotes.text: The key words MAY, MUST, MUST NOT, RECOMMENDED, SHOULD, and SHOULD NOT are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119].
When expanded, the resulting IRI MUST be a syntactically valid IRI [RFC3987].
A document SHOULD NOT define a mapping for the '_' prefix.
To ensure maximum consistency between processing environments, authors SHOULD remove any unnecessary white space in their plain and XML Literal content.

prefix
a white space separated list of prefix-name IRI pairs of the form

```
NCName ':' ' '+ xsd:anyURI
```

prefix      ::=   NCName

reference   ::=   ( ipath-absolute / ipath-rootless / ipath-empty ) 
                     [ "?" iquery ] [ "#" ifragment ] (as defined in [[!RFC3987]])

curie       ::=   [ [ prefix ] ':' ] reference

safe_curie  ::=   '[' [ [ prefix ] ':' ] reference ']'

Otherwise, if a CURIE consists of a non-empty prefix and a reference, and if there is an in-scope mapping for prefix (when compared case-insensitively), then the IRI is created by using that mapping, and concatenating it with the reference.
- Finally, if there is no in-scope mapping for prefix, then the value is not a CURIE.

TERMorCURIEorAbsIRI
- If the value is a term then it is evaluated as a term according to General Use of Terms in Attributes. Note that this step may mean that the value is to be ignored.
- If the value is a valid CURIE, then the resulting IRI is used.
- If the value is an absolute IRI, that value is used.
- Otherwise, the value is ignored.
quotes.note: Función: cómo se resuelven a IRI los valores de typeof y property; con ello se decide si el marcado RDFa es de Schema.org.

quotes.text: In all cases it is possible for these attributes to be used with no value (e.g., @datatype="") or with a value that evaluates to no value after evaluation using the rules for CURIE and IRI Processing (e.g., @datatype="[noprefix:foobar]").
quotes.note: Por qué no hay requisito de que los valores de typeof, property o resource se resuelvan: un valor que no da IRI está previsto y se ignora.
